name: כופלי לגרנז' – נפח מקסימלי של תיבה מתחת למישור (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Find the volume of the largest rectangular box in the first octant with three faces in the coordinate planes and one vertex on the plane \( {{CT:0}}x+{{CT:1}}y+{{CT:2}}z={{CT:3}} \)

[[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Maximize the volume \(V=xyz\) under the constraint \(g(x,y,z)={{CT:0}}x+{{CT:1}}y+{{CT:2}}z={{CT:3}}\) with \(x,y,z\ge 0\), using Lagrange multipliers. On the boundary of this region (a coordinate is 0) the volume is 0, so the maximum is at an interior critical point.
Step 1 — The maximum is at an interior point
The constraint set is the closed triangle cut from the plane by the first octant; it is closed and bounded and \(V\) is continuous, so \(V\) attains a maximum there. If one of \(x,y,z\) is 0 then \(V=0\), while for instance at \(x=y=z= rac{ {{CT:3}} }{ {{CT:4}} }\) the volume is positive. Hence the maximum is attained at a point with \(x,y,z\gt 0\), where the Lagrange condition holds.
Step 2 — Lagrange equations
\( abla V=\lambda abla g\) gives

\[ yz={{CT:0}}\lambda,\qquad xz={{CT:1}}\lambda,\qquad xy={{CT:2}}\lambda \]

Multiplying the three equations by \(x\), \(y\), \(z\) respectively, all left-hand sides become \(xyz\):

\[ xyz={{CT:0}}\lambda x={{CT:1}}\lambda y={{CT:2}}\lambda z \]

Here \(\lambda e 0\) (otherwise \(yz=0\)), so \({{CT:0}}x={{CT:1}}y={{CT:2}}z\). Substituting into the constraint, each of the three terms equals \( rac{ {{CT:3}} }{3}\):

\[ x= rac{ {{CT:3}} }{3\cdot {{CT:0}} }={{CT:5}},\qquad y= rac{ {{CT:3}} }{3\cdot {{CT:1}} }={{CT:6}},\qquad z= rac{ {{CT:3}} }{3\cdot {{CT:2}} }={{CT:7}} \]

Step 3 — The maximal volume
This is the only critical point with \(x,y,z\gt 0\), so it gives the maximum:

\[ V_{\max}={{CT:5}}\cdot {{CT:6}}\cdot {{CT:7}}={{CT:8}} \]

on_true.feedback:
Incorrect answer!

Since the rectangular box is in the first octant with three faces in the coordinate planes, the volume is calculated by the function \(V(x,y,z)=xyz\).

In order to satisfy of the restriction we substitute \( z={{CT:9}} \), which guarantees that one vertex is on the plane \({{CT:0}}x+{{CT:1}}y+{{CT:2}}z={{CT:3}}\) and we get the function \(V(x,y)=xy{{CT:9}}\).

Notice: The plane \( {{CT:0}}x+{{CT:1}}y+{{CT:2}}z={{CT:3}} \) has points on the first octant which are not on the coordinate planes. Therefore there's a point such that the volume of the rectangular is strictly greater than \(0\).

After calculating the system \( \left\{\begin{array}{cc}\frac{\partial V}{\partial x}(x,y)=0 \\\frac{\partial V}{\partial y}(x,y)=0 \end{array}\right. \) we get the critical points:

{{CT:10}}

Notice that only one point gives a volume which is strictly greater than \(0\). We get \(z={{CT:11}}\) and the correct answer is {{CT:12}}.
